paragraphs.text: Converted from an eighteenth-century hay barn, Willow Barn sleeps six in three bedrooms, one of which is on the ground floor with its own shower room, making it a sensible choice for guests who find stairs difficult. The open-plan kitchen has a range cooker and a dishwasher, and the enclosed garden backs onto a small stream. Well-behaved dogs are welcome, although we ask that no more than two stay at any one time and that they are kept off the furniture. The nearest village shop is a ten-minute walk along a footpath, but it closes at lunchtime on Sundays, so plan your weekend shopping accordingly. Changeover day is Saturday.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Owner Ffion Gallagher spent two years restoring The Old Schoolhouse, a Victorian building in Brindle Green, and the original classroom, with its high ceilings and tall arched windows, now serves as a generous living room. There are two double bedrooms upstairs, plus a sofa bed suitable for a child. Because the building is listed, open fires are not permitted, but underfloor heating keeps the house warm even in midwinter. Ffion lives in the next village and is happy to drop off a welcome basket of local bread, cheese and eggs if you let her know your arrival time in advance. Please note that the lane outside is narrow, and larger vehicles may find parking awkward.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Set right on the edge of the marshes at Lower Fenwick, Heron's Rest is a single-storey cottage ideal for birdwatchers and walkers. A pair of binoculars and a shelf of field guides are provided, and the living room window looks directly across the reed beds. The cottage sleeps four. There is no mobile signal at all in the area, although a landline is available for emergencies and the broadband connection works reliably in the kitchen. The track to the cottage can flood after heavy rain between November and February, so at that time of year the owner, Hamid Pereira, contacts guests the day before arrival to suggest a route on foot from the church car park. Wellington boots in several sizes are kept in the porch.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: This is not a cottage for everyone. Hilltop Bothy, on Carran Moor, has no road access: it is reached by a fifteen-minute uphill walk from the nearest parking area, and all supplies must be carried in. Electricity comes from solar panels, which provide enough power for lighting and charging phones but not for hairdryers or electric kettles; cooking is on a gas stove, and a wood-burner heats the single room. In return, guests enjoy what may be the finest views in the county and some of the darkest night skies. The bothy sleeps two, and bookings are for a minimum of three nights. Children under twelve cannot be accommodated because of the steep drop close to the door.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Families return to Orchard Cottage, in Stoke Abley, year after year. The large garden includes a climbing frame, a trampoline surrounded by safety netting, and an orchard where guests are free to pick apples and plums in season. Inside, there are four bedrooms, a games room with a table-tennis table, and a cupboard stocked with board games. A travel cot and a high chair can be supplied on request at no extra cost. The cottage is two miles from the nearest town, which has a supermarket, a swimming pool and a weekly farmers' market. Pets are not allowed, as the owners' hens roam the garden freely.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Perched on the cliffs above a sandy cove at Penmarrow Head, The Lookout was originally built for a coastguard and has been modernised by its current owner, Ruth Calloway, who added a glass-walled sitting room on the upper floor. Steps lead down from the garden gate to the beach, although they are steep and unsuitable for pushchairs. The cottage sleeps five and has a washing machine and an outdoor shower for rinsing off sand. Outside the school summer holidays, short breaks of two nights are accepted; in July and August, it is let by the week only. The coastal path passes the front door, and a café at the top of the cove serves breakfast from eight o'clock.
paragraphs.label: F

section.text:
Countryside Cottages to Rent This Season

A. Converted from an eighteenth-century hay barn, Willow Barn sleeps six in three bedrooms, one of which is on the ground floor with its own shower room, making it a sensible choice for guests who find stairs difficult. The open-plan kitchen has a range cooker and a dishwasher, and the enclosed garden backs onto a small stream. Well-behaved dogs are welcome, although we ask that no more than two stay at any one time and that they are kept off the furniture. The nearest village shop is a ten-minute walk along a footpath, but it closes at lunchtime on Sundays, so plan your weekend shopping accordingly. Changeover day is Saturday.

B. Owner Ffion Gallagher spent two years restoring The Old Schoolhouse, a Victorian building in Brindle Green, and the original classroom, with its high ceilings and tall arched windows, now serves as a generous living room. There are two double bedrooms upstairs, plus a sofa bed suitable for a child. Because the building is listed, open fires are not permitted, but underfloor heating keeps the house warm even in midwinter. Ffion lives in the next village and is happy to drop off a welcome basket of local bread, cheese and eggs if you let her know your arrival time in advance. Please note that the lane outside is narrow, and larger vehicles may find parking awkward.

C. Set right on the edge of the marshes at Lower Fenwick, Heron's Rest is a single-storey cottage ideal for birdwatchers and walkers. A pair of binoculars and a shelf of field guides are provided, and the living room window looks directly across the reed beds. The cottage sleeps four. There is no mobile signal at all in the area, although a landline is available for emergencies and the broadband connection works reliably in the kitchen. The track to the cottage can flood after heavy rain between November and February, so at that time of year the owner, Hamid Pereira, contacts guests the day before arrival to suggest a route on foot from the church car park. Wellington boots in several sizes are kept in the porch.

D. This is not a cottage for everyone. Hilltop Bothy, on Carran Moor, has no road access: it is reached by a fifteen-minute uphill walk from the nearest parking area, and all supplies must be carried in. Electricity comes from solar panels, which provide enough power for lighting and charging phones but not for hairdryers or electric kettles; cooking is on a gas stove, and a wood-burner heats the single room. In return, guests enjoy what may be the finest views in the county and some of the darkest night skies. The bothy sleeps two, and bookings are for a minimum of three nights. Children under twelve cannot be accommodated because of the steep drop close to the door.

E. Families return to Orchard Cottage, in Stoke Abley, year after year. The large garden includes a climbing frame, a trampoline surrounded by safety netting, and an orchard where guests are free to pick apples and plums in season. Inside, there are four bedrooms, a games room with a table-tennis table, and a cupboard stocked with board games. A travel cot and a high chair can be supplied on request at no extra cost. The cottage is two miles from the nearest town, which has a supermarket, a swimming pool and a weekly farmers' market. Pets are not allowed, as the owners' hens roam the garden freely.

F. Perched on the cliffs above a sandy cove at Penmarrow Head, The Lookout was originally built for a coastguard and has been modernised by its current owner, Ruth Calloway, who added a glass-walled sitting room on the upper floor. Steps lead down from the garden gate to the beach, although they are steep and unsuitable for pushchairs. The cottage sleeps five and has a washing machine and an outdoor shower for rinsing off sand. Outside the school summer holidays, short breaks of two nights are accepted; in July and August, it is let by the week only. The coastal path passes the front door, and a café at the top of the cove serves breakfast from eight o'clock.

questions.prompt: a restriction on the age of guests

explanation.en: Paragraph D says children under twelve cannot stay at the bothy. Paragraph F mentions that steps are unsuitable for pushchairs, but that is advice, not a rule about guests' ages.

explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що діти до дванадцяти років не можуть зупинятися в "bothy". В абзаці F згадано, що сходинки незручні для дитячих візочків, але це лише порада, а не правило щодо віку гостей.

explanation.uk: В абзаці A сказано, що сільська крамниця в неділю зачиняється в обід. Кафе з абзацу F — не крамниця, і для нього вказано лише час відкриття.

questions.evidence: contacts guests the day before arrival to suggest a route on foot from the church car park

explanation.en: Paragraph C says the track can flood in winter, so the owner tells guests about a walking route from the church car park.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что зимой дорогу может затопить, поэтому владелец рассказывает гостям о пешем маршруте от парковки у церкви.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що взимку дорогу може затопити, тому власник розповідає гостям про пішохідний маршрут від парковки біля церкви.

explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що Ffion Gallagher принесе кошик місцевих продуктів, якщо гості заздалегідь повідомлять їй, коли приїдуть.

questions.prompt: booking rules that change depending on the time of year
questions.evidence: Outside the school summer holidays, short breaks of two nights are accepted; in July and August, it is let by the week only

explanation.en: Paragraph F allows two-night stays except in July and August, when only whole weeks can be booked. Paragraph D has a minimum stay, but it is the same all year.
explanation.ru: Согласно абзацу F, можно остановиться на две ночи, кроме июля и августа, когда бронируются только полные недели. В абзаце D есть минимальный срок проживания, но он одинаков круглый год.
explanation.uk: Згідно з абзацом F, можна зупинитися на дві ночі, крім липня й серпня, коли бронюють лише повні тижні. В абзаці D є мінімальний термін проживання, але він однаковий цілий рік.
